channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from summarizedStoriesMainNLscienceAndDiscovery, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: Chemists free electrons and break a decades-old chemistry rule
item.description: A new catalyst allows chemists to break a long-standing rule about which molecules receive electrons in reactions, potentially opening new avenues in chemistry.

item.title: 60,000-year-old ostrich eggshell engravings reveal advanced human cognition
item.description: Ancient humans in southern Africa engraved ostrich eggshells with complex geometric patterns over 60,000 years ago, suggesting higher cognitive abilities than previously thought.

item.title: Dinosaurs grew huge, but why did they never evolve to be very small?
item.description: Dinosaurs dominated land at massive sizes, yet they rarely became truly tiny. New research points to physiological constraints that may have prevented miniaturization.

item.title: Bacteria found to convert toxic uranium into a stable, immobile form
item.description: Deep underground, certain bacteria may trap uranium before it spreads. In experiments, microbes fed uranium transformed it into a stable compound, potentially aiding cleanup.
